meta_description: Angelo Ortiz Vega — Technical Lead, Implementations at Silia, and AI Engineer based in Costa Rica. I make AI systems survive contact with production: LLM agents, evals, and real-time systems. 6 years across startups, consulting, banking, and enterprise logistics.
hero_txt_keywords: Technical Lead, Implementations · AI Engineer · Builder
hero_txt_about: I make AI systems survive contact with production. I work where client requirements, platform limits, and business commitments meet — LLM agents, evals, real-time systems, and the full stack that makes them usable.
about_text_desc_1: Hello! I'm Angelo Ortiz Vega — Technical Lead for Implementations at Silia, AI Engineer, and former University Lecturer from Costa Rica. I make AI systems survive contact with production: I sign off technical estimates, decide when an AI agent is ready to go live, and act as the technical counterpart to client IT teams. Before that, I led development on a logistics platform handling 220K weekly trips, where I drove the build of a real-time monitoring system unifying telemetry, vehicle, driver, and incident data — and designed the ETA prediction algorithm behind it.
about_text_desc_2: I'm a Computer Engineer from the Technological Institute of Costa Rica, with a foundation that runs deeper than web: FPGA and Verilog signal processing, CUDA parallel computing, computer architecture, and compilers. That background is why I'm drawn to software that touches the physical world — vehicles, sensors, telemetry, systems where something real depends on the output.

experience_text_subtitle: Roles where I've led and shipped products.
jobs_ucreativa: Taught industry-focused courses in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Data Analysis, Python, AWS, Full Stack Engineering, and User Experience Design to 250+ students across multiple cohorts, drawing directly from active production experience.
Mentored students through capstone projects and production-ready AI applications, guiding them from problem framing to deployed solutions using the tooling and practices teams use in industry.
Authored the complete UX Design Certification Program, from curriculum design to hands-on workshops and assessment.
Brought real-world case studies, agile delivery, and cloud infrastructure into the classroom, keeping course content aligned with what engineering teams are actually shipping.
jobs_silia: Own the technical solution for the Implementations area: sign off estimates, decide when an AI agent is ready to go live, and define the hypercare window for each release.
Act as the technical counterpart to client IT teams on integrations, access, infrastructure, and security.
Unblock the team when it hits a platform limit, distribute technical work across implementers, and escalate diagnoses — not symptoms — to the platform team.
Settle feasibility by testing, not opinion: stand up a test agent and verify end to end before answering whether something can be done.
Scope every PoC and demo in writing — what it shows, what it doesn't, and what is simulated — so it never turns into an unplanned commitment.
jobs_freelancer1: Delivered 15+ custom software solutions for startups, founders, and organizations — from marketing platforms and web applications to automation systems and cloud-native APIs.
Owned projects end-to-end: requirements discovery, solution architecture, development, deployment, and ongoing support, acting as the sole technical decision-maker.
Designed and shipped scalable systems with React, Node.js, Python, and AWS, integrating AI and automation where it removed real operational bottlenecks rather than adding complexity.
Worked directly with founders and business stakeholders to translate ambiguous business problems into maintainable, production-ready software under tight budget and timeline constraints.
Built custom integrations and automation pipelines that eliminated manual processes, cutting turnaround times and freeing client teams to focus on core operations.
jobs_creai_lead: Led technical direction for core business domains (routes, services, and trip management) on a large-scale logistics platform serving customers in Mexico.
Drove technical decisions, system design reviews, and implementation strategy across a cross-functional team of 20+ engineers, designers, product owners, delivery managers, and AI specialists.
Coordinated with Data Science and Product to move AI/ML capabilities from experimentation into production.
jobs_creai: Delivered AI-powered logistics products at scale: 220K weekly trips, 8.5K drivers, and 10K vehicles in production, with adoption measured against operational KPIs.
Led the development of a real-time monitoring system unifying driver, vehicle, telemetry, bucket, and incident data into a single live operational view.
Designed and implemented the ETA prediction algorithm powering that system, improving trip visibility and enabling proactive incident response across the network.
Shipped LLM-based agents and optimization algorithms integrated with legacy systems, turning fragmented manual processes into traceable, automated digital workflows.
Architected and maintained scalable full-stack applications and APIs with React, Ember.js, Laravel, PHP, and Python, bridging ML models and production systems end to end.
jobs_easyhop: Built the driver mobile application from the ground up, implementing route management, OpenStreetMap integrations, pickup workflows, and geolocation-based experiences.

Initiated and led a UX research effort with real drivers to understand how the product was actually used in the field — findings that reframed the team's MVP strategy and redirected development toward the passenger platform.

Joined the passenger web application team following that pivot, delivering business-critical functionality across frontend and backend and extending the product from a single mobile app into a multi-platform ecosystem.
Partnered with product stakeholders to translate user research into shipped features, improving route visibility, usability, and day-to-day operational workflows.
Grew from a mobile-focused role into full-stack product development, contributing across mobile, web, backend, and product strategy.
jobs_qubosystems: Served as technical lead for a payroll management platform built for a private university in Costa Rica, coordinating a team of 5 developers and owning architectural and implementation decisions end-to-end.
Designed and deployed a machine learning module that automated faculty salary classification, replacing a manual administrative process with a reproducible, auditable system.

Built a faculty information management platform that let academic staff maintain their own profile data and auto-publish to the university's public 'Claustro Docente' portal, eliminating a recurring editorial bottleneck.

Developed secure REST APIs, administrative platforms, and React frontends, including a data encryption module for a mobile point-of-sale solution used by a Costa Rican banking institution under financial-sector security requirements.

Delivered across the full software lifecycle — architecture, development, testing, deployment, and stakeholder collaboration — working directly with business teams to translate operational needs into shipped software.
jobs_csi: Performed corrective and preventive maintenance on industrial electrical equipment in a manufacturing plant.
Supported engineers in designing and developing electronic equipment to improve the cap production process.
Contributed to the plant's primary electrical maintenance plan.
projects_angelortizvcom: A space where I share what I'm learning and thinking, whenever I get a few minutes.
projects_easyhop: Problem: drivers had no single app to see routes, stops, and validate passenger tickets. I built the driver mobile app end-to-end — map with stop points, routes, and ticket validation — a core product the platform still uses today.
projects_topspinai: Problem: coaches and analysts had no automated way to analyze table tennis video for ball bounces and net hits. I built an AI system using computer vision — ball detection and semantic segmentation — that surfaces real-time insights from match footage.
projects_aiengineering: A structured knowledge base built chapter by chapter from Chip Huyen's AI Engineering (O'Reilly, 2025). Covers foundation models, evaluation, fine-tuning, and how to ship reliable AI applications to production — organized for quick review in reading order.
projects_uxarc: A personal blog and repository for knowledge, experiences, and resources on user experience design — organized to be accessible for anyone looking to sharpen their UX skills.
projects_ceitcr: Engineering projects from my Computer Engineering degree: FPGA/Verilog signal processing, CUDA parallel computing, cache coherence protocols, computer vision, and compiler design.
projects_ngClone: This is a Google Keep clone built with Angular to practice and improve my Angular skills. It follows the original app's design principles and includes many core features.
projects_karaoke: Karaoke is a project for the course SOA41D - Software Architecture. A simple Karaoke Streaming App build with React for the Front-end and Nodejs for Server-side.
projects_es369ims: Inventory Management System is an inventory service where products in stock are displayed through categories. Its data source is Excel, so that administrators can access the data more easily.
projects_itcrCourses: itcr-courses is the repository of my notes in the career of Computer Engineering. The principal purpose of this repository is record some of the data of the courses by the computer engineering degree program of the ITCR.
projects_spaceInvaders: Space Invaders is a Japanese shooting video game released in 1978 by Taito. In the original planning for the game, they had planned to have the aliens be human soldiers. Taito figured that they did not want to send the message that shooting humans was ok, so they changed it to aliens.
projects_pacman: Pac-Man is a 1980 maze action video game developed and released by Namco for arcades. I made a clone of the famous game in C ++ and Qt to apply concepts that I learned in courses on Algorithms and Data Structures.
